correctness.rationale: Average conjugates over simultaneous permutations of matched pairs and part interchange. This preserves feasibility and the uniform projector, and convexity ensures the centered norm cannot increase. In the averaged chain c=1−a−(m−1)b is the holding probability, and the cross block is (a−b)I+b11ᵀ. The centered nontrivial modes (part difference and the two paired zero-sum modes) have eigenvalues 2c−1, c+a−b and c−a+b, so the norm is max{|2c−1|,c+|a−b|}. Substituting b=(1−a−c)/(m−1), the latter linear modes are [(m−2)c+1−ma]/(m−1) and [mc+ma−1]/(m−1). Convex-combine 1−2c with each of these, choosing weights to cancel c. This gives unconditional lower bounds m(1−2a)/(3m−4) and (m−2+2ma)/(3m−2), including m=2 when the first mode's slope is zero. At their sole crossing a*=2/(3m) they equal 1/3. On the first branch the proposed b,c are nonnegative, c+a+(m−1)b=1, b≥a and c≤1/2; on the second the same checks hold with b≤a. The selected linear mode equals 1−2c on each branch, attaining the lower envelope of feasible objectives. The endpoints m=2,a=0 and a=1 retain the extra unit-modulus eigenvalues in the centered norm. For common bounds, the matched-edge average lies in [ℓ,u], and the strictly decreasing then increasing fixed-a response is minimized by clipping a*. This neither asserts uniqueness nor optimizes a finite-time distance. The frozen exact-rational checker was inspected, not run; these calculations prove the all-parameter result.

value.rationale: Fixing a distinguished partner link is a natural constraint in a two-class reversible network. The exact frontier quantifies how both inadequate and excessive use of such links harms mixing, identifies the switch between two spectral bottlenecks and tells when a permitted range incurs no cost. This is a useful all-size, all-capacity design law beyond the generic SDP and already-known endpoints.
